Through the Zeta Marketing Platform (ZMP), our vision is to make sophisticated marketing simple by unifying identity, intelligence, and omnichannel activation into a single platform – powered by one of the industry’s largest proprietary databases and AI. Our enterprise customers across multiple verticals are empowered to personalize experiences with consumers at an individual level across every channel, delivering better results for marketing programs. Zeta was founded in 2007 by David A. Steinberg and John Sculley and is headquartered in New York City with offices around the world. To learn more, go to www.zetaglobal.com.
THE ROLE
We’re a lean crew of business-savvy technologists who prototype first and perfect later. Our charter is to uncover opportunity, launch Version 0.1 in days, measure real-world impact, then iterate without ego. We mix cutting-edge tools with brilliantly low-tech hacks—whatever accelerates the outcome.
Automation is core to how we work. We’re looking for a builder who can spot repeatable pain, choose the right tools, wire systems together, and deliver automations that actually get used and create measurable value.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Identify and prioritize automation opportunities:
Partner with stakeholders to understand workflows, gather requirements, and continuously prioritize automation work based on impact (time saved, cost reduced, reliability improved).
Design end-to-end automation:
Select the right tools and patterns - serverless jobs, schedulers, cloud-native services, scripts, or AI-assisted workflows - and build solutions from first trigger to final outcome.
Build across the modern data stack:
Create and maintain automations spanning AWS, Azure, and Snowflake, integrating with APIs, data pipelines, and internal services.
Engineer production-ready jobs:
Write clean, reliable automation code using Python, SQL, C#, and TypeScript/JavaScript while handling scheduling, retries, logging, alerting, and failure modes.
Leverage AI where it makes sense:
Build automations both with and without AI integrations - using AI to accelerate classification, enrichment, validation, or decision-making when it delivers clear benefits.
Drive measurable outcomes:
Ensure every automation delivers value: track usage, validate impact, tune performance, and iterate or retire workflows based on real results.
Hunt for efficiencies:
Proactively spot manual steps, brittle processes, or expensive workflows and replace them with faster, cheaper, more reliable automation.
Raise the bar for everyone:
Document patterns, share reusable components, and help teams think more systematically about automation, creating systems instead of one-off scripts.
WHY ZETA'S DATA CLOUD ACCELERATION TEAM
Velocity.
Your GenAI ideas hit users in weeks.
Stack freedom.
No six-month procurement hurdles - pick the vendor or OSS model that fits.
Breadth.
Projects range from ad-tech optimization to identity resolution to creative signal mining.
Growth loop.
Every win feeds back into a playbook you own and evolve.
Distributed culture.
Work where you’re most effective - sync live when it matters, async when it doesn’t.
REQUIREMENTS
Experience building automations across cloud platforms (AWS and/or Azure) and modern data platforms like Snowflake.
Strong hands-on development experience with Python and SQL, with some experience in another language such as JavaScript or C#
Experience scheduling and orchestrating jobs (e.g., serverless functions, Airflow-like tools, cron-based systems, event-driven workflows).
Proven examples of automations that reduced cost, saved time, improved reliability, or unlocked new capabilities.
Experience integrating APIs, internal services, and third-party tools.
Familiarity with AI-assisted automation (LLMs, classification, extraction, decision support), with a pragmatic approach to when
not
to use AI.
Comfortable working end-to-end: requirements - design – build - deploy - measure.
You’ll thrive here if you…
Think pragmatically. You default to the simplest solution that works and scales.
Prototype quickly. You’d rather ship a working automation this week than debate frameworks for a month.
Care about outcomes. An automation that isn’t used or doesn’t deliver value isn’t “done.”
Translate easily. You can talk ROI with stakeholders and implementation details with engineers.
Love the blank canvas. Ambiguity is fuel, not friction.
Can cut through complex problems.
BENEFITS & PERKS
Unlimited PTO
Excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage
Employee Equity
Employee Discounts, Virtual Wellness Classes, and Pet Insurance And more!!
SALARY RANGE
The salary range for this role is

depending on location and experience.

framing analytical questions with the people who own the mission, and turning them into designs that can actually be tested;
building analyses and models in Python and SQL against a cloud-native data platform: Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL-compatible), Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) with Apache Iceberg tables, and related Amazon Web Services (AWS) analytics services;
designing the evaluation that provides the evidence a model is fit for a regulated environment: baselines, error analysis, and documented limits;
hardening one-off notebooks into repeatable, reviewed analytical pipelines; or
putting findings in front of decision-makers in plain language, with visuals that carry the argument instead of decorating it.

Soraban Connect is a product that bridges between our cloud platform and the desktop tax software that CPA firms actually run (UltraTax, Lacerte, and several others) that were never designed with APIs or automation in mind. Connect comprises a Windows application, a backend API service, and automation scripts that programmatically drive this software to eliminate hours of manual data entry per return.
This is automation against software that actively resists being automated. It's some of the most interesting engineering work we do since there’s no obvious, straight and narrow path. It requires creative thinking to build workarounds and solutions that can be messy. When it works, accountants get days of their lives back during tax season.
What you'll do
Build and extend automation that controls professional tax software, navigating UIs programmatically, moving data reliably, and handling the thousand edge cases real tax returns produce
Make automation resilient. Tax software vendors ship updates that break things. You'll build the testing, monitoring, and tooling that catch breakage early and make fixes fast, turning fragile scripts into dependable infrastructure
Develop the backend API service (Python) that coordinates between our cloud platform and the desktop world
Improve the Windows application (Python) that firms install and run including packaging, updates, and the local runtime that hosts the automation

3+ years of professional software engineering experience, with strong Python
Experience with UI, browser, or desktop automation (Selenium, Playwright, pywinauto, AutoHotkey, or you rolled your own — we care about the intuition, not the tool)

Comfort working on and targeting Windows environments

Interest and drive to dive into unfamiliar territory and deliver
Nice to have
Experience with tax, accounting, or fintech software

Windows application packaging, installers, or code signing
Experience making flaky systems reliable (retries, idempotency, observability)

Default to action: Move quickly and iterate. Progress over perfection. Learn by shipping.

Ownership from day one. Small team, no layers. The automation you build ships to real firms, and you'll see the impact directly

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. Job Description
We are seeking an experienced SAP BTP Integration Suite Developer with functional testing capabilities in SAP S/4HANA. The ideal candidate understands both the technical data orchestration layer within BTP and the functional flow of procurement processes within S/4HANA to independently execute, troubleshoot, and validate integration scenarios.
Key Responsibilities
Design & Development: Architect and develop end-to-end integration flows (iFlows) using SAP BTP Integration Suite (Cloud Integration/CPI, API Management).
Interface Mapping: Design complex data transformations (XML, JSON, Flat Files) to align S/4HANA enterprise structures with Source-to-Pay cloud platform data models.
S/4HANA Functional Testing: Independently execute end-to-end testing by simulating and triggering business processes directly within S/4HANA (e.g., creating Purchase Requisitions, releasing Purchase Orders, posting Goods Receipts/Invoices).
Data Validation: Verify that master data (Suppliers, Cost Centers, Gl Accounts, Material Master) and transactional data sync accurately between S/4HANA tables/OData services and Source-to-Pay cloud platform.
Troubleshooting & Debugging: Diagnose integration failures across the entire stack—analyzing BTP runtime logs, checking S/4HANA application logs (SRT_UTIL, SM58, SLG1), and reviewing Source-to-Pay cloud platform API responses.
Collaboration: Partner with business analysts and Source-to-Pay cloud platform IT to define test cases, build test scripts, and drive User Acceptance Testing (UAT).
Required Technical & Functional Skills
SAP BTP Integration Suite: 3–5 years of hands-on experience building iFlows, configuring adapters (OData, SOAP, IDoc, SFTP), and utilizing Groovy Script/JavaScript.
S/4HANA Functional Competency: Working knowledge of SAP MM (Materials Management) and FI (Financial Accounting) modules.
SAP Testing Toolset: Ability to navigate S/4HANA UIs (Fiori/GUI), use standard transaction codes (e.g., ME21N, MIGO, MIRO, BP), view database tables (SE16N), and utilize debugging/monitoring tools.
Cloud Procurement Connectivity: Experience interfacing middleware Source-to-Pay cloud platforms (Ivalua, Coupa, Ariba) via REST/SOAP APIs and file-based transfers.
Modern SAP Integration Protocols: Deep understanding of S/4HANA standard APIs, OData V2/V4 services, and standard Enterprise Services alongside traditional IDocs.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with automated testing tools or Postman for API testing.
SAP Certification in BTP Integration Suite or S/4HANA Sourcing & Procurement.

description_preview:
Company Overview:
Pronoia Energy is a pioneering deep tech startup at the forefront of quantum energy storage innovation. As a lean, mission-driven team, we thrive on rapid prototyping, cross-disciplinary collaboration and solving complex engineering challenges to turn quantum physics into practical, scalable products. Our current focus is on developing our groundbreaking room-temperature macroscopic quantum energy storage technology that promises orders of magnitude greater energy density, faster charging, and higher power delivery as well as being cheaper and safer compared to existing battery technology. This represents a paradigm shift in energy storage with applications spanning consumer electronics, electric vehicles, renewable grids, and beyond.
Role Summary
:
To meet our ambitious goals we are hiring an Embedded Systems Engineer to write the low-level software that runs directly on our hardware and makes our experiments and our product do exactly the right thing, every time. This is a hands-on role in a high-stakes, high-reward startup environment where reliability is not optional. In this role you will develop the firmware that controls sensors, measurement, actuation, and safety in real time. Because a battery safety cutoff cannot be a little late, you will work within strict, guaranteed timing limits, building the control and safety logic that keeps energetic hardware behaving predictably. You will partner closely with our electrical engineer on board bring-up and with the science team on instrumenting experiments, turning our experimental rigs and the product's own control electronics into dependable systems. This role is onsite in Torrance, California.
Key Responsibilities:
Write and maintain firmware for the control and safety electronics of our cells and test hardware.
Implement real-time control loops, safety interlocks, and data acquisition.
Bring up new boards and integrate sensors, measurement, and actuation.
Partner with the electrical engineer on hardware-software bring-up and with the science team on experimental instrumentation.
Contribute to troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of hardware-software problems.
Required Qualifications:
3+ years of experience developing firmware that controls real physical hardware (motors, sensors, power stages), not only desktop software.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
Strong C and C++ and microcontroller experience.
A real understanding of real-time constraints and safety interlocks.
Experience debugging hardware-software problems with instruments in hand, such as an oscilloscope or a logic analyzer.
A self-starter who is comfortable with ambiguity and rapid pivots in a startup setting.
Preferred Qualifications:
Flight-software, avionics, or scientific-instrument firmware background.
Experience writing control or data-acquisition software for measurement equipment.
A reliability mindset shaped by a real field failure and the process changes that followed.
Prior work in deep tech R&D alongside interdisciplinary teams.
What We Offer:
Chance to solve one of the world's biggest engineering challenges and pioneer quantum energy storage.
Competitive salary, equity in a transformative startup, and performance-based incentives.
Access to cutting-edge labs, tools, and resources in a flexible, collaborative work environment.
Comprehensive benefits: health insurance, unlimited PTO, professional development stipend, and relocation assistance if needed.
A culture of innovation where your work will accelerate our path to market impact.
If you're excited to tackle this real-world quantum problem and build the energy systems of the future, apply with your resume and cover letter detailing relevant projects.

Company Overview:
Pronoia Energy is a pioneering deep tech startup at the forefront of quantum energy storage innovation. As a lean, mission-driven team, we thrive on rapid prototyping, cross-disciplinary collaboration and solving complex engineering challenges to turn quantum physics into practical, scalable products. Our current focus is on developing our groundbreaking room-temperature macroscopic quantum energy storage technology that promises orders of magnitude greater energy density, faster charging, and higher power delivery as well as being cheaper and safer compared to existing battery technology. This represents a paradigm shift in energy storage with applications spanning consumer electronics, electric vehicles, renewable grids, and beyond.
Role Summary:
To meet our ambitious goals we are building an internal, grounded, agentic AI system that accelerates our research, and we are hiring a Platform and Infrastructure Engineer to build the body and nervous system it runs on. This is a foundational, high-reward role for someone who makes a system both reliable and locked-down at the same time. In this role you will turn our owned hardware, an on-premises AI computer and database, into a real working platform: reliable local model serving, an on-prem database that serves as both the search index and the provenance and audit store, and a sandboxed execution environment where AI-generated code runs without reaching the internet or touching sensitive data. The single most important instruction in this role is to bake trust-boundary discipline into the codebase from day one, so that hardening it into a fully locked-down enclave later is a migration, not a rewrite. This role is onsite in Torrance, California.
Key Responsibilities:
Build reliable local model serving and data infrastructure on owned, on-premises hardware.
Stand up a sandboxed code-execution environment with default-deny networking.
Implement the provenance and audit store that records where every fact came from.
Design the early system already shaped like the secure end-state, with data-classification and boundary discipline built in.
Wear several hats as a founding generalist and later hand specialties to dedicated hires.
Required Qualifications:
Deep backend and systems engineering with genuine bare-metal or on-premises experience, not cloud-only.
Real sandboxing and untrusted-code-isolation depth, for example network namespaces, seccomp, or egress filtering.
A security instinct that shows up as default-deny defaults and auditable, versioned infrastructure.
Comfort being a founding generalist who later hands specialties to dedicated hires.
A self-starter who thrives amid ambiguity and rapid iteration.
Preferred Qualifications:
A defense, aerospace, or regulated-data background that makes the enclave mindset second nature.
Experience running your own GPU fleet rather than renting cloud compute.
Familiarity with containerization, orchestration, and GPU-serving infrastructure.
Prior work in deep tech R&D alongside interdisciplinary teams.
What We Offer:
Chance to solve one of the world's biggest engineering challenges and pioneer quantum energy storage.
Competitive salary, equity in a transformative startup, and performance-based incentives.
Access to cutting-edge labs, tools, and resources in a flexible, collaborative work environment.
Comprehensive benefits: health insurance, unlimited PTO, professional development stipend, and relocation assistance if needed.
A culture of innovation where your work will accelerate our path to market impact.
If you're excited to tackle this real-world quantum problem and build the energy systems of the future, apply with your resume and cover letter detailing relevant projects.

Direct experience with AI/HPC infrastructure, including NVIDIA GPUs, InfiniBand or high-speed Ethernet fabrics, and related management software (e.g., NCCL, SLURM).
Experience with advanced observability and monitoring systems (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) for complex, high-cardinality telemetry data.

Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements).
Familiarity with SLOs/metrics measurement, logs/telemetry/metrics integration with tools for enhanced operator experience.

description_preview:
About Radar
Radar is the global leader in geolocation, with geofencing SDKs, maps APIs, and AI-enabled solutions for marketing, fraud, and operations teams.
Why is Radar the best place to work?
We're trusted by some of the world's best companies, from high-growth startups to the Fortune 500.
We have incredible scale: We're processing over 1 billion API calls per day from hundreds of millions of devices.
We're well-resourced, and we've raised $85.5M from world-class investors, including Accel and Insight Partners.
We have a high-performance culture, with ambitious and entrepreneurial teammates in every role.
We recently moved into an amazing new office in Flatiron, Manhattan, NYC.
We were recently named a top 10 best place to work in NYC by Crain's.
Despite our growth and scale, we're still just getting started. That's where you come in.
About The Role
We're looking for Product Engineers to build features across multiple mobile stacks. Over the past year, our SDKs have been installed on over 100M devices worldwide and our steady state traffic is 10,000 qps. Our SDKs are open-source (
Android
,
iOS
), abstracting away cross-platform differences between location services and allowing you to add geofencing, location tracking, and maps to your apps with just a few lines of code. You'll also work on our demo apps, including "Waypoint," an app used internally and by customers to test the Radar SDK.
How We Work
Most of our engineering team are former technical co-founders or former Radar interns from schools like Waterloo and CMU. Most engineers at Radar fit one of two molds, technically: either Staff level expertise in one stack, or "Multi-Stack" at any level. We say "Multi-Stack" because "Full-Stack" has the connotation of "Frontend and Backend", but Radar Engineers might also work on Mobile or Data engineering. Not that you need to be an expert in all of those, but a desire to learn, jump around to different stacks, and get things done is the important part.
We care a lot about shipping fast and talking to customers. We're committed to our product vision of full-stack location infrastructure, but we also know that customer feedback is a treasure map to gold. Even though Slack is the brain of our company, working together in-person in our NYC HQ is the fastest way for us to get things done. We meet on Mondays to plan out work for the week in small groups and use Linear for planning. All projects are run by an Engineering lead, an executive and a Go-to-Market lead. Engineers figure out what to build, talk to customers, talk to prospects, help close them, get them live and make them successful.
One of our most important company values is "Walk a mile," as in walking a mile in the customer's shoes, but also as in literally walking a mile, getting up from your desk and developing a deep understanding of how location services behave in the real world. To us, a week is a long time, and we expect to ship big things every week.
The Stack
Our mobile stack includes Kotlin, Objective-C, and Swift. We also have thin cross-platform SDK wrappers for React Native, Capacitor, Flutter, and few others.
We sponsor OpenStreetMaps, MapLibre, and OpenAddresses.
How We Use AI
Engineers choose what AI tools they use, Claude and Codex being the most popular.
We're actively building Claude skills - for example we've taught it how to debug HorizonDB, our geospatial database.
All code changes are reviewed by an Engineer knowledgeable in that area. Claude and Codex also review all PRs.
There is a range of how much engineers use AI. Most use it daily if not weekly.
We are excited about what AI can do, but we also recognize the risks and don't compromise our coding standards.
The Hiring Process
After a call with our Technical Recruiter, you'll do several technical Zoom calls with members of our engineering team: code screen, coding round, and system design round. If those go well we'll invite you to our NYC HQ for a final round interview. You'll meet one of our co-founders, someone from outside engineering, and meet more people from Radar. We'll go into more depth about how we work to see if there is a match.
What You’ll Do
Work on core Radar mobile infrastructure built with Kotlin, Objective-C, Swift, as well as wrapper SDKs written in React Native, Flutter and Capacitor. (Android SDK, iOS SDK)
Embody our "Walk a mile" value by walking around to QA and debug the Radar SDK
Push the limits of what is possible with location services on iOS and Android
Have your work run on 100's of millions of devices
Talk to Radar customers and prospects, hear their feedback, incorporate it into your work and make them successful
You Should
Have experience building Mobile infrastructure
Don't think of yourself as an "iOS Engineer" or "Android Engineer"
Are interested in talking to customers or prospects and making them successful
Are deeply curious about how things work, and have the tenacity to sit with hard problems and power through them
Bonus Points If You
Are a former technical co-founder
Have worked on an SDK
Have experience with Indoor positioning
Have experience with background location or network infrastructure with respect to Doze mode, Wake Locks, Background Execution Limits, App Standby Buckets, and Foreground Services
Have experience with FusedLocationProvider, GeofencingClient and Beacon monitoring and ranging
You’ll Work With
Nick Patrick, Co-Founder and CEO
Tim Julien, CTO
Liam Meier, Director of Engineering
Our customers and prospects
Our Customer Success, Sales Engineering, and Sales teams

New HQ in Flatiron, NYC

Health, dental, and vision insurance with 100% coverage for employees
12 weeks of paid parental leave
Commuter and fitness benefits

title: Full-Stack "Readiness" Software Engineer

description_preview:
Soraban is a Series A startup automating the most painful parts of tax season for CPA firms. Our platform handles client data collection, document delivery, and tax workflow automation for firms across the country — and we're growing fast. We're a small, fast-moving engineering team where everyone ships, everyone owns what they build, and there's no committee between a good idea and production.
Readiness Role
Most engineering teams ask every engineer to be two people at once: the fast-moving explorer who figures out what to build, and the systems thinker who makes it scale, perform, and survive contact with real users. We've split those into two roles.
Discovery Engineers figure out what to ship — they prototype fast, validate with users, and prove out product ideas. Readiness Engineers — this role — take those validated prototypes and make them real: the right architecture, the right data models, performant, scalable, and secure. Depending on the project, that means taking a clean handoff and rebuilding from the ground up, pairing with a Discovery Engineer through the transition, or working embedded alongside them from early on.
If you're the engineer who's mildly offended by a missing index, an N+1 query, or an unvalidated input — the one who finds genuine satisfaction in taking something that
works
and making it something that
lasts
— this role was designed for you. This isn't cleanup work. It's the craft half of product engineering, given the focus and respect it rarely gets.
What you'll do
Productionize validated prototypes. Take working v1s and design artifacts from Discovery Engineers and build the production version: architecture, data models, and implementation that will hold up under growth
Own performance and scale. Our traffic is intensely seasonal — tax season is our Super Bowl, and it lasts four months. Systems you build need to hold up when every firm hits crunch at once
Make security a property, not a patch. We handle sensitive taxpayer data for CPA firms, and security is a first-class engineering requirement here — you'll build it in from the data model up
Set the technical bar. Your architectural decisions, data modeling, and code become the foundation other engineers build on. The patterns you establish compound
Polish the front-end until it feels finished. Prototypes prove the idea; you'll refine the React/Next implementation until the details hold up — responsive edge cases, loading and error states, accessibility, and the small interactions that separate "works" from "feels professional"
What we're looking for
5+ years of professional software engineering experience
Strong systems judgment — data modeling, query performance, background processing, caching, and the architecture instincts that come from having scaled real products (our stack is Ruby on Rails with React/Next)
Security-minded engineering habits — you think about authorization, input validation, and data exposure by default, not as an afterthought
The temperament for this role: you genuinely enjoy hardening, refining, and finishing — depth over novelty
Strong collaboration instincts — this role lives at a handoff boundary, and making that boundary work takes clear communication, not just clean code
A fast ramp. You'll join a mature codebase with real users, and we expect (and support) senior engineers contributing meaningful work within their first few weeks — not after a quarter of onboarding
Nice to have
B2B SaaS or fintech background — especially products handling sensitive data
Experience with compliance-adjacent engineering (SOC 2 environments, audit-friendly design, PII handling)
Experience with seasonal or spiky-traffic systems
History of successfully rebuilding or replatforming systems that started as prototypes
How we work
Our values aren't wall art. They describe how decisions actually get made here:
Mission focused: The mission is our north star. We stay focused on what moves it forward and tune out the noise.
Default to action: Move quickly and iterate. Progress over perfection. Learn by shipping.
Solve with data: Instinct gets us asking the right questions — data gets us to the right answer.
Automate first: Automate the repetitive work so we can focus where we add the most value. (This role is this value.)
Why this role
A role designed around a real specialty. Most companies treat production engineering as what happens after the interesting work. We made it the job — with the autonomy and scope to do it right
Ownership from day one. Small team, no layers. The systems you build ship to real firms, and you'll see the impact directly
Series A momentum. We've found product-market fit with CPA firms and are scaling. Joining now means growing with the company, not maintaining someone else's decisions
In-person team in Chandler. We work together in the office — fast feedback loops, real whiteboards, no meeting-scheduling purgatory
Logistics
Full-time, in-office in Chandler, AZ
Health, dental, and vision coverage
401(k)
Paid time off

description_preview:
Your Journey at Crowe Starts Here:
At Crowe, you can build a meaningful and rewarding career. With real flexibility to balance work with life moments, you’re trusted to deliver results and make an impact. We embrace you for who you are, care for your well-being, and nurture your career. Everyone has equitable access to opportunities for career growth and leadership. Over our 80-year history, delivering excellent service through innovation has been a core part of our DNA across our audit, tax, and consulting groups. That’s why we continuously invest in innovative ideas, such as AI-enabled insights and technology-powered solutions, to enhance our services. Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.
Job Description:
About the Role· We work on medium-term machine learning projects (1-6 months) with a high degree of autonomy.
In order to further the Data Science Team strategic imperative of having a “Culture of reuse: tools, products, and processes.”, the primary strategy of the Toolkit Team will be to develop generalizable tools for common problems and facilitate the sharing of code within/between projects.
Work within the Data Science Team to define common problems and identify opportunities in the existing codebase to solve current and future problems
Develop libraries and services to address common requirements for our machine learning products
Collaborate with data scientists to get their machine learning models from prototype to production
Champion the use and adoption of Toolkit libraries and services
Required Skills - Programming experience. Your job will require you to code. We mainly write in Python, so experience in this language is preferred. Familiarity with another lower-level language (C/C++, Go, etc) is a plus Software engineering experience. You enjoy software engineering and know your way around algorithm design and data structures. You are comfortable working in Linux-based systems and are familiar with using Docker to develop and deliver RESTful APIs. Additional experience in areas such as cloud computing, distributed systems, CI/CD, etc., is a plus. Capacity for autonomy. You won’t be on your own on day one, but you will need the capacity to manage your time between research and tool development. Strong communication skills. You are comfortable adjusting how you discuss software engineering projects, from the technical details to high-level concepts, depending on your audience of software engineer teammates, data scientist collaborators, and non-technical business stakeholders.
Adaptable. Toolkit problems will involve different areas of computer science and machine learning skills, sometimes within the same problem. You can context shift depending on the problem and can adjust if new problems and/or requirements arise requiring rethinking the approach to solving a problem.
Detail oriented. Toolkit is focused on making tools that just work. You like to find edge cases and potential bugs in code, you go above and beyond developing use cases beyond the requested basics, and you are meticulous with following software engineering best practices, including writing maintainable code with clear documentation and comprehensive test cases.
Skills to Stand Out. You like to code and have interest in learning new technologies. You find it exciting to explore and/or improve libraries to help you solve a problem. Lifelong engineering. You want to stay up to date with regards to practicing engineering and you strive for continuous learning and improvement.
Curiosity about machine learning. You know a few things about learning algorithms, data preprocessing strategies, or some other interesting areas of machine learning that can help create more integrated and robust software solutions.
Outside field. You have an educational, research, or hobby background in an interesting area of software engineering, computer science, or related field that you believe gives you unique skills for approaching software engineering and/or machine learning problems
Essential Job Functions:
responsible for executing on tasks to achieve their project’s overarching technical vision.
Responsibilities vary across the development lifecycle from supporting client intake conversations and conducting data exploration for new projects to ongoing feature development and bugfixes to support mature machine learning products in a software release cycle.
effectively execute on tasks for your assigned project(s) with some direction and support; your code quality reflects the team's standards.
Working within a finance and accounting firm, recognize and appropriately escalate risks and support assigned mitigations.
You support your team members' growth through pair programming, code review, and/or knowledge sharing.
We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.
Crowe accepts applications for this role on an ongoing basis.
In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.
The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Crowe, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. Job Description:
About the Role· We work on medium-term machine learning projects (1-6 months) with a high degree of autonomy.
In order to further the Data Science Team strategic imperative of having a “Culture of reuse: tools, products, and processes.”, the primary strategy of the Toolkit Team will be to develop generalizable tools for common problems and facilitate the sharing of code within/between projects.
Work within the Data Science Team to define common problems and identify opportunities in the existing codebase to solve current and future problems
Develop libraries and services to address common requirements for our machine learning products
Collaborate with data scientists to get their machine learning models from prototype to production
Champion the use and adoption of Toolkit libraries and services
Required Skills - Programming experience. Your job will require you to code. We mainly write in Python, so experience in this language is preferred. Familiarity with another lower-level language (C/C++, Go, etc) is a plus Software engineering experience. You enjoy software engineering and know your way around algorithm design and data structures. You are comfortable working in Linux-based systems and are familiar with using Docker to develop and deliver RESTful APIs. Additional experience in areas such as cloud computing, distributed systems, CI/CD, etc., is a plus. Capacity for autonomy. You won’t be on your own on day one, but you will need the capacity to manage your time between research and tool development. Strong communication skills. You are comfortable adjusting how you discuss software engineering projects, from the technical details to high-level concepts, depending on your audience of software engineer teammates, data scientist collaborators, and non-technical business stakeholders.
Adaptable. Toolkit problems will involve different areas of computer science and machine learning skills, sometimes within the same problem. You can context shift depending on the problem and can adjust if new problems and/or requirements arise requiring rethinking the approach to solving a problem.
Detail oriented. Toolkit is focused on making tools that just work. You like to find edge cases and potential bugs in code, you go above and beyond developing use cases beyond the requested basics, and you are meticulous with following software engineering best practices, including writing maintainable code with clear documentation and comprehensive test cases.
Skills to Stand Out. You like to code and have interest in learning new technologies. You find it exciting to explore and/or improve libraries to help you solve a problem. Lifelong engineering. You want to stay up to date with regards to practicing engineering and you strive for continuous learning and improvement.
Curiosity about machine learning. You know a few things about learning algorithms, data preprocessing strategies, or some other interesting areas of machine learning that can help create more integrated and robust software solutions.
Outside field. You have an educational, research, or hobby background in an interesting area of software engineering, computer science, or related field that you believe gives you unique skills for approaching software engineering and/or machine learning problems

responsible for executing on tasks to achieve their project’s overarching technical vision.

effectively execute on tasks for your assigned project(s) with some direction and support; your code quality reflects the team's standards.

Job Description:
About the Role· We work on medium-term machine learning projects (1-6 months) with a high degree of autonomy.
In order to further the Data Science Team strategic imperative of having a “Culture of reuse: tools, products, and processes.”, the primary strategy of the Toolkit Team will be to develop generalizable tools for common problems and facilitate the sharing of code within/between projects.
Work within the Data Science Team to define common problems and identify opportunities in the existing codebase to solve current and future problems
Develop libraries and services to address common requirements for our machine learning products
Collaborate with data scientists to get their machine learning models from prototype to production
Champion the use and adoption of Toolkit libraries and services
Required Skills - Programming experience. Your job will require you to code. We mainly write in Python, so experience in this language is preferred. Familiarity with another lower-level language (C/C++, Go, etc) is a plus Software engineering experience. You enjoy software engineering and know your way around algorithm design and data structures. You are comfortable working in Linux-based systems and are familiar with using Docker to develop and deliver RESTful APIs. Additional experience in areas such as cloud computing, distributed systems, CI/CD, etc., is a plus. Capacity for autonomy. You won’t be on your own on day one, but you will need the capacity to manage your time between research and tool development. Strong communication skills. You are comfortable adjusting how you discuss software engineering projects, from the technical details to high-level concepts, depending on your audience of software engineer teammates, data scientist collaborators, and non-technical business stakeholders.
Adaptable. Toolkit problems will involve different areas of computer science and machine learning skills, sometimes within the same problem. You can context shift depending on the problem and can adjust if new problems and/or requirements arise requiring rethinking the approach to solving a problem.
Detail oriented. Toolkit is focused on making tools that just work. You like to find edge cases and potential bugs in code, you go above and beyond developing use cases beyond the requested basics, and you are meticulous with following software engineering best practices, including writing maintainable code with clear documentation and comprehensive test cases.
Skills to Stand Out. You like to code and have interest in learning new technologies. You find it exciting to explore and/or improve libraries to help you solve a problem. Lifelong engineering. You want to stay up to date with regards to practicing engineering and you strive for continuous learning and improvement.
Curiosity about machine learning. You know a few things about learning algorithms, data preprocessing strategies, or some other interesting areas of machine learning that can help create more integrated and robust software solutions.
Outside field. You have an educational, research, or hobby background in an interesting area of software engineering, computer science, or related field that you believe gives you unique skills for approaching software engineering and/or machine learning problems
Essential Job Functions:
responsible for executing on tasks to achieve their project’s overarching technical vision.
Responsibilities vary across the development lifecycle from supporting client intake conversations and conducting data exploration for new projects to ongoing feature development and bugfixes to support mature machine learning products in a software release cycle.
effectively execute on tasks for your assigned project(s) with some direction and support; your code quality reflects the team's standards.
Working within a finance and accounting firm, recognize and appropriately escalate risks and support assigned mitigations.
You support your team members' growth through pair programming, code review, and/or knowledge sharing.
We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.
Crowe accepts applications for this role on an ongoing basis.
In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. Crowe is not sponsoring for work authorization at this time.
The wage range for this role takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. The disclosed range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. At Crowe, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. In order to further the Data Science Team strategic imperative of having a “Culture of reuse: tools, products, and processes.”, the primary strategy of the Toolkit Team will be to develop generalizable tools for common problems and facilitate the sharing of code within/between projects.
Work within the Data Science Team to define common problems and identify opportunities in the existing codebase to solve current and future problems
Develop libraries and services to address common requirements for our machine learning products
Collaborate with data scientists to get their machine learning models from prototype to production
Champion the use and adoption of Toolkit libraries and services
Required Skills - Programming experience. Your job will require you to code. We mainly write in Python, so experience in this language is preferred. Familiarity with another lower-level language (C/C++, Go, etc) is a plus Software engineering experience. You enjoy software engineering and know your way around algorithm design and data structures. You are comfortable working in Linux-based systems and are familiar with using Docker to develop and deliver RESTful APIs. Additional experience in areas such as cloud computing, distributed systems, CI/CD, etc., is a plus. Capacity for autonomy. You won’t be on your own on day one, but you will need the capacity to manage your time between research and tool development. Strong communication skills. You are comfortable adjusting how you discuss software engineering projects, from the technical details to high-level concepts, depending on your audience of software engineer teammates, data scientist collaborators, and non-technical business stakeholders.
Adaptable. Toolkit problems will involve different areas of computer science and machine learning skills, sometimes within the same problem. You can context shift depending on the problem and can adjust if new problems and/or requirements arise requiring rethinking the approach to solving a problem.
Detail oriented. Toolkit is focused on making tools that just work. You like to find edge cases and potential bugs in code, you go above and beyond developing use cases beyond the requested basics, and you are meticulous with following software engineering best practices, including writing maintainable code with clear documentation and comprehensive test cases.
Skills to Stand Out. You like to code and have interest in learning new technologies. You find it exciting to explore and/or improve libraries to help you solve a problem. Lifelong engineering. You want to stay up to date with regards to practicing engineering and you strive for continuous learning and improvement.
Curiosity about machine learning. You know a few things about learning algorithms, data preprocessing strategies, or some other interesting areas of machine learning that can help create more integrated and robust software solutions.
Outside field. You have an educational, research, or hobby background in an interesting area of software engineering, computer science, or related field that you believe gives you unique skills for approaching software engineering and/or machine learning problems

WHO WE ARE
Lockheed Martin is a global leader in aerospace, defense, and technology solutions, dedicated to pushing the boundaries of innovation and shaping the future of the industry. With a rich legacy of excellence and a commitment to delivering advanced capabilities to our customers, we are proud to be at the forefront of cutting-edge technology and engineering.
LM SPACE: WHAT WE'RE DOING
Space is a critical domain, connecting our technologies, our security and our humanity. While others view space as a destination, we see it as a realm of possibilities, where we can do more — we can innovate, invest, inspire and integrate our capabilities to transform the future.
At Lockheed Martin Space, we aim to harness the full potential of space to cultivate innovation, reduce costs, and push the boundaries of what technology can achieve.
THE WORK
Lockheed Martin is seeking a talented Level 2 Ground Software Engineer with an active Final Top Secret security clearance to work from our King of Prussia, PA location.
We are looking for software engineers to craft and build innovative solutions for our customers. You will be part of an Agile team that utilizes state of the art commercial standard methodologies such as DevSecOps (automated testing, continuous integration, automated deployment, etc.) and modern development tools.
You will participate in progressing system capabilities from early design through site acceptance focused on software reuse, COTS/FOSS integrations, and innovative, affordable best practices. You will support modernization efforts geared toward achieving greater efficiency, security, automation and scalability
You will collaborate with an enthusiastic team of software, systems, and test engineers using the Agile Development methodology

Ensures software standards are met.

Software Development, Software Engineering background, with a track record of successful project delivery
Experience in Scaled Agile development methodologies, with excellent communication skills for effective collaboration and teamwork across Agile Development Teams.
Active TS Clearance required for consideration with the ability to obtain an SCI.

Cloud/containerization experience with a good understanding of distributed systems and designing for scalability
Experience developing ground subsystems
Experience developing microservices
Proficient in using Git for version control and collaboration
Working knowledge of DevSecOps Pipelines
Excellent understanding of Agile Methodologies as they relate to the Scaled Agile Framework
Experience with Agile, automated test, CI/CD, and regression testing
Committed with strong problem-solving skills applied to software engineering solutions
Previous experience delivering highly reliable Communications / Ground subsystems

Full-Time Salary Range: $91200.00 - $169400.00

Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.
Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.
We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.
Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.

description_preview:
This is a job that Jill, our AI Recruiter, is recruiting for on behalf of one of our customers.
She will pick the best candidates from Jack's network.
The next step is to speak to Jack.
Job Title
Forward Deployed Engineer
Salary
Not Disclosed
Company Description
CommodityAI is building the AI-powered operating system for the global commodities industry, automating the complex manual workflows across the energy, metals, and agricultural sectors.
Job Description
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at CommodityAI, you will bridge the gap between AI product and physical trade operations. You'll partner with customers to automate unstructured data flows, configure technical schemas, and drive successful deployments. This is a high-impact role for an engineer who thrives at the intersection of code and customer outcomes.
Location
San Francisco, USA
Why this role is remarkable
Work at the epicenter of global trade, transforming the foundational sector responsible for moving the world’s energy, metals, and agricultural resources.
Join a high-growth environment where the product is selling faster than it can be onboarded, offering massive scale and impact.
Gain high-agency experience with direct mentorship from the founding team while building the company's deployment playbooks from the ground up.
What You Will Do
Configure data schemas and AI extraction workflows to turn messy real-world documents and emails into structured, actionable trade data.
Lead customer onboarding workstreams from initial scoping and technical configuration through to user acceptance testing and successful go-live.
Build internal tools, scripts, and automation templates that accelerate the deployment process and create leverage for the entire engineering function.
The ideal candidate
1-3 years of experience in software engineering, implementation engineering, or a technical consulting role with strong coding skills in Python or TypeScript.
Proven technical proficiency with APIs, structured data models, and the ability to diagnose complex issues across AI-driven systems.
Exceptional communication skills and an operator mindset, comfortable managing multiple customer workstreams in a fast-paced, early-stage startup environment.
Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.
Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.
We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.
Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.

The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Identity team builds, operates, and innovates the identity, authentication, and authorization stack for the AWS cloud. Our mission is to push the technical boundaries to enable AWS customers to run their business workloads confidently and securely. As part of this mission, AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) enables customers to securely share their AWS resources across accounts, organizations, and organizational units — simplifying multi-account governance while maintaining fine-grained access controls.
AWS RAM allows customers to centrally manage resource sharing at scale, eliminating the need to create duplicate resources in every account. As AWS grows and customers adopt increasingly complex multi-account strategies, RAM must evolve to support new resource types, richer sharing policies, and higher-order scalability demands. We are looking for strong software engineers to build the next generation of resource sharing infrastructure. Individuals interested in this position should have experience building high-performing, reliable systems in a distributed, multi-tenant environment at a fast pace.

You care deeply about API design that makes complex sharing workflows intuitive — making "the right thing, the easy thing." You think about the customer experience when weighing engineering trade-offs, whether that's designing retention behaviors for departing accounts, enabling resource discovery, or ensuring consistent state across asynchronous workflows. You value operational excellence — advocating for actionable alarms, eliminating toil, and squashing flaky tests before they erode confidence. You also believe that having fun and tackling hard problems go hand-in-hand: event-driven architectures, eventual consistency challenges, high-throughput resource indexing, and building APIs that scale to millions of shared resources — all while maintaining the security and reliability customers depend on.

Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.

We’re looking for a software engineer to own the engineering side of support. When something breaks, you’re the one who picks it up, works out what’s actually going on, and drives it to a fix. Your job is to respond fast and keep everyone in the loop until it’s closed. Camps run their whole operation on the product in season, so quick response times are what the role lives and dies by.
It’s a full engineering role, not a ticket queue. Between the bugs you’re shipping features and improvements in the same codebase, in the same standups and reviews as the rest of engineering.
What we expect
We’re Not Asking You To Fix Everything The Instant It Arrives. Some Bugs Are Quick. Some Are Deep. Some Turn Out To Be a Config Issue Or a Missing Feature, Not a Bug At All. What We Expect Every Time Is a Fast, Honest Response And Clear Coordination:
The camp always knows their issue has been picked up and what happens next
You’ve triaged it: real bug, config problem, or feature gap, and routed it accordingly
If it’s a fast fix, you ship it. If it’s bigger, you scope it, log it in Linear, and help pull in the right people
Nothing goes quiet. The status is always visible to the team and the customer
Proactive beats heroic here. We’d rather you flag a problem early and set the right expectation than promise a same-day fix on something that genuinely takes three days.
What you’ll do
Pick up camp-reported bugs, reproduce them, and drive them to resolution at whatever pace each one honestly allows
Triage fast and accurately: separate real bugs from configuration and feature requests, and route each to the right owner
Ship the fixes you can, and scope and coordinate the ones you can’t do alone
Ship features and improvements between bug work, so you’re building on the roadmap and not only firefighting
Work across the stack: React with Inertia on the front, Ruby on Rails behind it, Postgres for data
Watch our error monitoring tools and catch issues before a camp has to report them
Track everything in Linear, and join the same standups, reviews, and Slack as the rest of engineering to help curate the product
What we’re looking for
Comfortable across frontend and backend in a Rails and React codebase
You enjoy dropping into unfamiliar code and tracing a bug to its cause without any hand-holding
A clear communicator who sets expectations well. You’ll read customer reports and often talk to camps directly
Available through US business hours, since in-season issues need same-day attention even when the fix takes longer
Real hands-on coding experience and a solid grasp of what you’re shipping. AI speeds you up, but it doesn’t do the job for you, so this isn’t a role for someone who only vibecodes
Fluent with AI tools like Claude Code and Codex, and clear-eyed about where they help and where they don’t
You know camp, or you want to. Understanding how a camp actually runs helps you fix the right things first, and camp experience of any kind is a plus
Logistics
Remote, US-based
Working hours may shift later during the summer season, depending on your timezone, to cover camps while they’re live
In peak season, expect to be reachable for urgent issues outside normal hours from time to time
Potential travel for industry events (e.g. ACA Tri-State, Camp Collab, and similar)
What we offer
Salary of $90,000
Health coverage
Budget to set up your home office: desk, monitor, chair, whatever helps you work well
About Campfront
Campfront is a camp management platform for US summer camps. Camps use it to run enrollment, payments, and the daily admin of operating a camp.
Campfront is a new platform with an experienced team behind it. It comes from the people who built Camp Leaders, drawing on more than 25 years running programs and working with camp directors.
We hire great people, trust them with real ownership, and back them with modern tools. The team is lean and autonomous by design, which is how we ship weekly and move fast. We have fun doing it, and we take real pride in building the best software in the industry and setting a new bar for what camps should expect.

As a Software Development Engineer, you will play a crucial role in the development of services to support the automation of the Leo mission. description_preview:
This is a job that Jill, our AI Recruiter, is recruiting for on behalf of one of our customers.
She will pick the best candidates from Jack's network.
The next step is to speak to Jack.
Job Title
Full-Stack Engineer
Salary
$140k-$170k
Company Description
Chahalo is a rapidly growing modern tea brand bringing the authentic Chinese tea experience to New York City with four locations across Manhattan and Queens. Building their technology function from the ground up, Chahalo bridges the gap between traditional retail and modern digital consumer experiences through custom-built internal and external tools.
Job Description
As the first engineering hire at Chahalo, you will lead the development of the company’s digital foundation. You’ll design and build the consumer ordering platform, loyalty programs, and internal operational tools from the ground up. This greenfield role offers total ownership over the technical direction while directly impacting thousands of customers across New York City.
Location
New York City, USA
Why this role is remarkable
Founding Engineer Opportunity: As the first technical hire, you will have a greenfield opportunity to architect and build the entire digital infrastructure from scratch.
Physical-Digital Integration: Your work will directly power four physical locations in NYC, creating a seamless bridge between digital ordering and the premium in-store tea experience.
High Impact and Visibility: Work closely with the founder to define the product roadmap and technical strategy for one of the city's fastest-growing consumer brands.
What You Will Do
Develop consumer-facing applications including a high-performance web ordering platform and a custom customer loyalty program using React and Node.js.
Architect and maintain the backend infrastructure and database schema using PostgreSQL to support inventory management, store operations, and data analytics.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of features, from initial technical design and API development to deployment and monitoring in production environments.
The ideal candidate
3–5 years of professional experience building and shipping consumer or B2B products end-to-end using TypeScript, React, Node.js, and PostgreSQL.
Demonstrated ability to work independently in a high-growth startup environment, comfortably handling ambiguity and making high-level architectural decisions without an existing roadmap.
Strong proficiency in modern web frameworks and tools, with specific experience in Next.js and GraphQL being highly preferred for building scalable consumer interfaces.
Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.
Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.
We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.
Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.

Overview
Being good neighbors – helping people, investing in our communities, and making the world a better place – is who we are at State Farm. It is at the core of how we operate and the reason for our success. We're moving with urgency to become a Next Gen Good Neighbor, with technology that strengthens human connections and enhances the customer experience. As an employee, you'll spend less time navigating systems and more time applying judgment, empathy, and expertise in the moments that matter most.
HYBRID
Qualified candidates must live within a
180-mile radius
of a hub location listed below and should plan to spend time working from home and some time working in the office as part of our hybrid work environment
.
HUB LOCATIONS: Bloomington, IL; Richardson, TX; Atlanta, GA; or Tempe, AZ
SPONSORSHIP:
Applicants for this position are required to be eligible to lawfully work in the U.S. immediately; employer will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work authorization (e.g. H-1B visa) for this opportunity.
Responsibilities
Grow Your Skills, Grow Your Potential
Are you passionate about enhancing customer experiences through innovative solutions? Do you enjoy problem-solving and improving communications? Join our team and help craft the documents customers receive from State Farm!
We’re seeking a Software Engineer or a Lead Software Engineer for our batch Design & Development and On-Demand Composition Modernization teams within the Customer Communications product suite. You’ll collaborate with business, infrastructure, and application teams to design, develop, test, and support batch and on-demand applications using the OpenText Exstream composition toolset. Our team creates high-volume, customer-facing communications such as policy documents, renewal notices, billing statements, claim correspondence, and important notices—delivered by mail or online—while maintaining design and development standards to ensure quality.
This role supports the modernization of our communication tools, including adoption of cloud technologies. You’ll have meaningful opportunities to improve customer interactions across insurance and financial services products.
If you value quality, teamwork, and making an impact, we’d love to hear from you!
Qualifications
Required Skills
These skills are essential for day-to-day success in this role:
Prior software engineering and programming experience
Experience with composition software, preferably OpenText Exstream or similar tools, including shared components and content import functionality
Familiarity with data dictionaries and Exstream driver files
Experience with code repositories, shared forms, version control, and deployment of package files to testing and production environments
Understand the concept of APIs and JSON payload schemas
Understanding of API testing tools such as Postman or Insomnia
Understanding of or experience with different output formats (e.g., AFP, PDF)
Strong knowledge of data structures (e.g., XSD, XML, JSON) and data merge techniques
Ability to assess impacts on upstream and downstream processes, including troubleshooting
Awareness of coding standards for accessibility compliance
Desired Skills
These skills are a plus and will help you excel and grow in the position:
Understanding of Customer Communication Management (CCM) practices
Understanding of unit testing concepts and frameworks
Object-oriented programming experience; JavaScript or Python skills
Experience with additional OpenText Exstream tools (e.g., Communications Designer, Content Author, Empower)
Experience with agile development methodologies
Our Benefits
Because work-life balance is a priority at State Farm, compensation is based on our standard 38:45-hour work week!
Potential starting salary range: $100,000 - $140,000
Starting salary will be based on skills, background, and experience
High end of the range limited to applicants with significant relevant experience
Potential yearly incentive pay up to 15% of base salary

Get Paid! On top of our competitive pay, you are eligible for an annual raise and bonus.
Stay Well! Focus on you and your family’s health with our robust health and wellbeing programs. State Farm pays most of your healthcare premium, and we offer multiple healthcare plan options, including a high deductible plan. All medical plans provide 100% coverage for in-network preventative care, AND you and your family have access to vision, dental, telemedicine, 24/7 mental health professionals, and much more!
Develop and Grow! Take advantage of educational benefits like industry leading training programs, top-notch tuition assistance programs, employee resource groups, and mentoring.
Plan Ahead! Plan for those big moments in life with benefits like fertility/IVF/adoption assistance, college coaching, national discount programs, interactive monthly financial workshops, free financial coaching, and more. You can also start a savings account or consider financing through our State Farm Federal Credit Union!
Take a Little “You” Time! You will have access to our generous time off policies designed so you can plan around holidays, family events, volunteering, or just to take a relaxing day off. With the opportunity to initially earn up to 20 days annually plus parental leave, paid holidays, celebration day, life leave (40 hours/year), bereavement leave, and community service/education support days, there will be plenty of time for you!
Give Back! We offer several ways to give back through our Matching Gift Program, Good Neighbor Grant Program, and the Employee Assistance Fund.
Finish Strong! Plan for retirement using free financial advisors and a 401(k) plan with company contributions of up to 7% of your salary.

description_preview:
This is a job that Jill, our AI Recruiter, is recruiting for on behalf of one of our customers.
She will pick the best candidates from Jack's network.
The next step is to speak to Jack.
Job Title
Software Engineer - Core Financial Platform
Salary
$180k-$275k + Equity
Company Description
Basic Capital is a $25M Series A fintech based in SoHo, NYC, backed by Lux Capital and Forerunner Ventures. They are rebuilding the infrastructure of America’s $1T retirement industry, creating a fundamentally new retirement system powered by a team of elite engineers from Stripe, Uber, and Goldman Sachs.
Job Description
As a Software Engineer on the Core Financial Platform team, you will design and build the high-reliability systems responsible for moving money at scale. You will architect event-driven workflows, design reconciliation logic, and own the infrastructure for trading and fund management, ensuring the transparency and reliability that modern retirement investing requires.
Location
New York, USA
Why this role is remarkable
Work directly with an elite team of senior engineers who have built mission-critical financial systems at scale for companies like Stripe, Square, and Uber.
Tackle deep technical challenges by rebuilding retirement infrastructure from the ground up, replacing decades-old legacy systems with modern, transparent, event-driven architectures.
Join a high-impact, $25M Series A startup backed by top-tier investors like Lux Capital, Forerunner Ventures, and Henry Kravis in a high-performance SoHo office.
What You Will Do
Architect and build core trading, financing, and fund management systems that orchestrate and reconcile complex flows of funds with high reliability.
Design and implement event-driven backend systems and asynchronous workflows using tools like Kotlin, Temporal, and modern cloud infrastructure.
Participate in high-level architecture discussions and code reviews, maintaining complete ownership of mission-critical transaction systems from design to production.
The ideal candidate
Has 3+ years of experience building distributed, high-reliability backend systems and event-driven architectures using languages like Kotlin, Go, or Rust.
Demonstrates strong expertise in relational databases like PostgreSQL/MySQL and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP), with a focus on correctness and system reliability.
Thrives in a fast-paced, high-agency environment and is excited to work in-office in SoHo to solve complex social and financial problems.
Who are Jack & Jill?
Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.
And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.
How does this work?
Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.
We never post fake jobs
This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.
Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.
We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.
Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.
